title: How To Fix Hero Photo Not Showing on Your Website
author: Reconnect Master
description: How to troubleshoot and fix the issue of a hero photo not displaying on your website.
content: If you're experiencing issues with your hero photo not displaying on your website, here are some common causes and solutions.
## Common Causes
1. **Incorrect Image Path**: The most common issue is an incorrect file path to the image.
2. **Image File Not Found**: The image file might be missing or moved.
3. **CSS Styling Issues**: CSS rules might be hiding the image or affecting its display.
4. **Server Configuration**: Some server configurations might block certain image types or locations.
## Check one image before changing everything
Open your browser, using a real file name:
Example: https://yourwebsite.com/public/images/posts/photo.png
The picture should have loaded if the path above is correct.
## If it does NOT load, check these:
The deploy finished. Wait a couple of minutes after pushing,
then hard refresh with **Ctrl + F5**.
The file name matches exactly. **GitHub Pages is case-sensitive**, go check that Photo.png, and photo.png are different files. Also are .png and .jpg.
The image was pushed. Look for it in your repository on GitHub, since an image that only exists on your computer won’t show.
## Alternative:
Move **images/** out of **public/** to the root of the project
and keep **/images/posts/photo.png** in the JSON.
Both approaches work, so pick one and stay consistent.
## Troubleshooting Steps
### 1. Check the Image Path
Ensure the image path in your HTML is correct:
```html ```
### 2. Verify Image File Existence
Make sure the image file exists at the specified location and has the correct name and extension.
### 3. Inspect CSS Styles
Use browser developer tools to inspect the image element and check if any CSS rules are hiding it or affecting its display.
### 4. Test Server Configuration
If you're using a CMS or a custom server setup, ensure that the server is configured to serve image files correctly.
## Other Cases:
For example, if you have a file named **photo.png** in a folder **public/images/posts/**, then
Your images are in:

```json
"/public/images/posts/photo.png"
```
Instead of:

```json
/images/posts/photo.png
```
which would show a **broken image**.
That shortcut belongs to build tools and frameworks like: **Astro, Vite, Next.js and similar**
which copy the contents of public/ to the top of the website when they build it.
However, if your site is plain HTML hosting such as GitHub Pages does no building
The real address of each image still includes **public**.
### The fix: add **public** to the path in each JSON file

```json
"image": "/public/images/posts/photo.png"
```
This works on the live site and in **Live Server**, so your local preview will match.
If the above steps do not resolve the issue, consider checking for browser caching issues.
